chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadlal, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from al-Fadl ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari and Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from one of them, who said:

Regarding a man who has a pregnant wife and wishes to divorce her: He divorces her when he intends the divorce, with the testimony of witnesses. If it occurs to him on that day or afterwards that he wishes to take her back (revocation), he shall take her back with the same [conditions], and he shall consummate. Then if it occurs to him, he divorces her again. Then if it occurs to him, he shall take her back as he took her back the first time. Then if it occurs to him, he divorces her; she is the one who does not become lawful to him until she marries a husband other than him, if he is the revoking one who intends consummation and retention, and he consummates.

key_terms.الرّجعَة: Revocation (taking back the wife during the waiting period)

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for a man to divorce his pregnant wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain clarifies the mechanics of *Talaq al-Munajjaz* (irrevocable divorce) for a pregnant wife, emphasizing that the husband must explicitly intend each revocation (*Raj'a*) and subsequent divorce (*Talaq*) to ensure validity. It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction that the finality of the divorce, which necessitates *Nikah al-Mut'ah* or *Nikah al-Mu'assas* with another man before remarriage, is contingent upon the husband's conscious intent at each stage, rather than a fixed count alone.
